title: Protocol for editing fibroblasts with in vitro transcribed Cas9 mRNA and profile off-target editing by optimized GUIDE-seq
protocol: Check the map of plasmid which will be used as the DNA template and chose proper digestion enzyme to linearize this plasmid.
Determine recommended digestion buffer, plasmid amount (optimally: 8000 ng), reaction incubation time and temperature based on chosen enzyme.
Run the digestion reaction at 37°C for 15 minutes according to obtained information.
Run agarose gel to check linearization quality and product size.
Thaw HiScribe T7 ARCA mRNA Kit components, mix and pulse-spin in microfuge to collect solutions.
Take 1 μg of linearized plasmid and assemble reaction in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube following kit instructions.
Mix thoroughly and pulse-spin in a microfuge.
Incubate at 37°C on heat block for 30 min.
Add 2 μL of DNase I to each tube from previous step.
Mix well and incubate at 37°C for 15 min.
The Poly(A) tailing reaction can be set up in each tube from the previous step.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min.
Save 1 μL for analysis if necessary.
Add 25 μL of LiCl solution (7.5 M Lithium Chloride, 0.05 M EDTA) to the 50 μL transcription reaction.
Mix well.
Incubate at -20°C for 30 min or longer.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 15 min at top speed (>12000 rpm) of a microcentrifuge to pellet the RNA.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Rinse the pellet by slowly adding 500 μL of ice-cold 70% ethanol to remove residual salt, and then centrifuge at 4°C for 10 min.
Remove the ethanol carefully.
Spin the tube briefly to bring down any liquid on the wall.
Remove any residual liquid carefully with a sharp pipette tip (e.g., 10 μL).
Air dry the pellet – a white or transparent pellet of the RNA will form within few minutes (do not dry more than 10 min).
Resuspend the mRNA in nuclease-free water.
Make aliquots in PCR tubes, label and store the mRNA at -20°C (less than 6 months) or -80°C (more than 6 months).
Add 1 g agarose in 72 mL water and heat until dissolved.
Cool the mixture to 60°C.
In the fume hood, add 10 mL of 10× MOPS running buffer to the agarose solution.
In the fume hood, add 18 mL of 37% formaldehyde (12.3 M) to the agarose solution.
Mix gently but thoroughly by inverting the bottle several times without introducing bubbles.
Pour the gel into a plastic chamber and insert a gel comb with wells large enough to accommodate at least 25 μL.
Note: If any bubbles are formed, remove them by poking with a small pipette tip.
Let the gel solidify for at least 2 h in the fume hood.
Assemble the gel in the tank and add enough 1× MOPS running buffer to cover the gel.
Add no more than 5 μL of the sample RNA to a 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 3 volumes of Formaldehyde Load Dye to the sample RNA.
Incubate the samples for 15 min in a 65°C water bath to denature any RNA secondary structure.
Briefly spin down samples in a microcentrifuge and place on ice.
Add 0.5 μL ethidium bromide to the samples to visualize the RNA directly during and after electrophoresis.
Load the samples on a denaturing formaldehyde agarose gel using RNase-free pipette tips.
Place the tip just inside the top of the well.
Expel the sample slowly.
Gently raise the tip out of the well.
Load the RNA size markers on the gel.
Run the gel with 10V voltage per centimeter of distance between electrodes.
Stop electrophoresis when the bromophenol blue dye front has migrated approximately 3/4 the length of the gel.
Use a computer-controlled CCD camera system with a UV transilluminator to photograph the gel.
Pre-program the electroporation unit.
Turn on the Core Unit of Lonza 4D-Nucleofector.
Follow the instruction of the instrument.
Select the wells that will be electroporated.
Set the “Solution” and “Plus Code” accordingly.
Leave the instrument at this state for now.
Check the cells for confluency.
Aspirate cell culture medium in T-175 flask.
Wash cells once with 35 mL pre-warmed PBS.
Aspirate PBS.
Add 15 mL pre-warmed Trypsin into the flask.
Incubate at 37°C for 5 min until all cells have detached.
Gently tap the flask and confirm proper dissociation using a microscope.
Add pre-warmed cell culture medium up to 30 mL.
Pipette up and down using a 25 mL pipette.
Check under microscope for cell presence.
Transfer cell suspension into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 300×g (RCF) for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1000 μL pre-warmed cell culture medium using a 1000 μL pipette.
Fill up to 10 mL with pre-warmed cell culture medium.
Take an aliquot for counting.
Mix 10 μL Trypan Blue and 10 μL cells.
Count with Countess II.
Take the required volume of cells for electroporation gently.
Prepare mRNAs, sgRNA and ssDNA repair template and Cas9WT RNP in 96-well PCR plate.
Take out Cas9 RNAs from −80°C (or –20°C) and place on ice.
Let Cas9 RNAs thaw completely.
Take out sgRNA(s) and ssDNA repair template(s) and place on ice.
Let sgRNA(s) and ssDNA repair template(s) thaw completely.
Place a sterile 96-well plate into the hood.
Pipette 1 μL of target gene sgRNA (100 μM) into each needed well for electroporation.
Add 1 μL of IDT Cas9WT protein (60 μM) to wells containing sgRNA to form RNPs.
Cover the plate with tinfoil and briefly spin.
Mix gently by scraping over the bottom of the 96-well plate.
Incubate at room temperature for 15 min.
Place on ice.
Add 1 μL of ssODN repair template (100 μM) into each well containing RNPs or sgRNA only.
Cover the wells with foil and place on ice until use.
Spin the cells for 5 min at 300g.
Remove supernatant, add 30 mL of warm PBS, wash gently.
Spin once more for 5 min at 300g.
Remove PBS and resuspend in an appropriate volume of electroporation buffer (20 μL/well).
Pipette 20 μL of cell suspension in electroporation buffer onto the plate containing sgRNA, RNPs, and ssODNs.
Mix briefly.
Keep the plate on a cooling rack at 4°C.
Pipette mRNAs onto corresponding test wells using a 100 μL pipette.
Use ethanol and RNase Away spray to clean the hood environment for sterility of the mRNA.
Load 20 μL into corresponding wells of the electroporation strip(s)/plate(s).
Check for bubbles in the electroporation strips/plates.
Gently tap with the strips/plates on the bench or palm of hand.
Proceed with electroporation.
Press “START” and perform electroporation.
Transfer the electroporation strip(s)/plate(s) back to the hood.
Add 80 μL of pre-warmed full cell culture media (without Penicillin and Streptomycin, P&S) into each well of the strip(s)/plate(s).
Place the electroporation strip(s)/plate(s) into the incubator for 15 minutes.
Prepare the cell culture plate(s)/dish(es) with full cell culture medium (without P&S).
After 15 minutes, place back the strip(s)/plate(s) into the bench.
Distribute the cell suspension from electroporation strip(s)/plate(s) into corresponding wells of the cell culture plate(s).
Make a crisscross movement with the culture plate(s) to ensure equal distribution of cells.
Check the cell culture plate(s) under the microscope and place into the incubator.
Remove old media from previous day and add warm one with P/S.
Harvest sample 4 days after electroporation (if counting electroporation day as day-1, then harvest on day-5).
Extract genome DNA from harvested samples.
Profile off-target editing by optimized GUIDE-seq method on Day 2 and Day 7–10.
Use dsODN probes and ddPCR to find the optimal concentration of dsODN for GUIDE-seq.
Profile off-target editing with the GUIDE-seq method.
Optimize the dsODN concentration according to the cell type.
Transfect cells with double-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (dsODN).
Identify off-target cleavage/gene editing sites in a genome-wide manner.
Anneal two modified oligonucleotides in the same way as annealing the Y adapter.
Design Affinity Plus (IDT) probes for dsODN used in GUIDE-seq.
Test different amounts of dsODN in cells undergoing CRISPR-Cas9 editing to optimize dsODN concentration.
Consider the electroporation transfection buffer system for the experiment.
Dissolve dsODN to achieve a concentration of 1 μM in 20 μL electroporation transfection buffer (20 pmol in total).
Monitor cell viability daily after dsODN transfection until samples are harvested.
Add dsODN together with other reagents just before electroporation for editing fibroblasts with Cas9 mRNA.
Include a group of blank cells as a control.
Include a group of cells only treated with dsODN as a background control.
Include a group of edited cells without added dsODN to serve as a negative control for dsODN integration.
Mix 10 μl Trypan Blue with 10 μl cells suspension.
Count the mixture using Countess to determine cell viability and amount of living cells/mL.
Trypsinize adherent cells into a single-cell suspension before counting if necessary.
Check and record cell viability in each condition every day until cells are harvested.
Determine editing efficiency at the gene editing target by ddPCR after sample harvesting.
Dilute gDNA in 1× TE Buffer to a final volume of 100 μL in 0.65 mL Bioruptor Microtubes for shearing.
Vortex samples (5–10 s) and centrifuge (10 s) before shearing.
Store samples on ice during 5–10 min prior to sonication.
Shear gDNA using the “7 cycles, 15 s ON / 90 s OFF” condition according to the standard operating protocol for the Bioruptor Pico Sonicator at 4°C water cooler temperature.
Run undiluted sheared gDNA samples (5 μL) with a 1.2% agarose gel and image it to check size and quality of gDNA if necessary.
Take 400 ng of sheared gDNA and bring the final volume to 120 μL using 1× TE Buffer.
Clean up samples with 120 μL of AMPure XP SPRI beads (1× ratio).
Perform AMPure XP purification according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Elute purified samples in 15 μL of 1× TE Buffer.
Add the required components for end-repair and A-tailing reactions as per the protocol.
Mix well by brief vortexing, and spin down.
Place the tube or plate on a thermocycler machine.
Set the end repair thermocycler program as specified.
Proceed with adapter ligation after completion of the end-repair thermocycle program.
Add reagents in order as specified for each reaction tube or well (mix by pipetting).
Put the tube/plate on thermocycler machine and set the adapter ligation program accordingly.
Clean using 0.9× Ampure XP SPRI beads after adapter ligation.
Elute cleaned sample in 12 μL of 1× TE buffer.
Optional: Run a control sample on agarose gel to check Y adapter_MI addition.
Prepare PCR master mix as specified for each reaction (Discovery or Deep-sequencing Validation).
Proceed with separate PCR reactions for Discovery (+ and -) using separate master mixes.
